newsitem.title: ITALY: Mother Teresa is "unstoppable engine" - Rome mayor.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa is "unstoppable engine" - Rome mayor.

text.p: Rome mayor Francesco Rutelli said after an hour of talks with Mother Teresa of Calcutta on Sunday that she was as vigorous as ever and in fine form.

"I found her extraordinarily well," Rutelli said after meeting the 86-year-old nun at the Rome branch of her Missionaries of Charity order. "I found the same energy...Mother Teresa is an unstoppable little engine."

Fears about Mother Teresa's fragile health were raised when she flew into Rome on Friday from New Delhi and needed oxygen for about 20 minutes. But doctors said the procedure was normal for a woman of her age after a long trip and she was fine.

Rutelli said Mother Teresa, who has undergone three heart operations and stepped down in March as superior-general of her order because of ill-health, greeted him warmly in the courtyard and left her wheelchair to sit in the shade in an armchair. Doctors were on hand as a precaution.
She used the meeting to ask for a hospitality centres for homeless people and AIDS patients in Rome to be enlarged and other centres to be improved. Rutelli said he had agreed.

Mother Teresa, known as the saint of the gutters for her devotion to the poor, is expected to meet Pope John Paul and present to him the new head of her order, Sister Nirmala. A date for the meeting has not yet been set.
